notes: OpenCode 2.x through the service API (#2109 P5b-1). Two session-end variants in one run: v1 is archived (the reader reports the row gone: transcript_removed); v2 ends when the service exits (SIGTERM inside the maintainer-approved service window): process_exited on the service pid, in ready. The TTL end was measured in P3's QA run 2 and is not re-recorded.

text: The API session is admitted when its first activity lands (P3, #2107): a ses_… transcript_new. Its first state is not pinned — an API session is first seen working (P4; P5a's smoke cells)
The session binds to the one running 2.x service (pid.go servicePIDFor) — there is no client process
v1's prompt drives it to working
The 2.x plugin's session.execution.succeeded ends turn 1 (recorded as the canonical Stop hook)
v1 ends by archive: the reader no longer lists it and reports it gone, while it is in ready
v2: a NEW ses_… session at the same location, admitted on its first prompt
v2's prompt drives it to working
The 2.x plugin's session.execution.succeeded ends turn 2 (recorded as the canonical Stop hook)
v2 ends by service exit: the daemon reports its pid gone and drops the session from ready — it never goes working after the exit
